_comment_1: The 'Scan Resolution in DPI', with possible values of 100 and above, corresponds to the resolution, in dots per inch (DPI), of the scanned scoresheet JPEG files located in the 'Scans' subfolder. A scan resolution of 200 DPI gives small file sizes and works reasonably well in terms of accuracy. You might want to scan your drawings at a higher DPI setting to potentially increase the accuracy of the color prediction (default setting: 200).
_comment_2: The 'Brightness Level' corresponds to the extent to which the R, G and B values (each between 0 and 255) will be lightened or darkened (for negative brightness values). It can be useful to bring the brightness down, such as to bring the darkest gray value close to zero, thus creating more headspace to spread out the remaining colors during the contrast step (default setting: 0, or no changes).
_comment_3: The 'Contrast Level' setting will adjust the contrast level of the JPEG scan images, with a contrast level of one resulting in no changes, a value less than one and greater than zero decreasing the contrast, and a value above one increasing the contrast. Increasing the contrast using a setting of around 1.1-1.2 can spread out the colors to make them easier to distinguish (default setting: 1.0, or no changes).
_comment_4: The 'Paper Color Filter Threshold', with possible values spanning from 0 to 255, inclusively, will determine the R, G and B value cutoff point above which the pixels on the brightness- and contrast-adjusted image will be set to 255, with the other pixels remaining the same. For example, a threshold of 245 would set all the R, G and B pixel values lighter than it (greater than 245) to 255 and the other R, G and B pixel values would be unchanged (default setting: 255, or no changes).
_comment_5: The 'A4 or US Letter Format Selection' will indicate which paper format, A4 or US Letter, is to be used when generating the graph paper PDF template and when processing your scans (default setting: US Letter).
_comment_6: The 'Graph Line Pixel Width', with possible values of 1 or above, will determine the line width in pixels of the lines making up the graph paper grid of the PDF template, at a resolution of 300 dpi (default setting 3).
_comment_7: The 'Thicker Graph Line Pixel Width', with possible values of 1 or above, will determine the line width in pixels of the bold lines drawn at a regular interval in the graph paper grid of the PDF template, at a resolution of 300 dpi (default setting 5).
_comment_8: The 'Number of Squares Between Thicker Lines', with possible values of 0 (no bold lines) or above, will determine the number of squares between bold lines in the graph paper grid of the PDF template (default setting: 5).
_comment_9: The 'Graph Line RGB or Hex Code Color' will set the color of the lines of the graph paper grid of the PDF template. The color needs to either be specified as an RGB value (e.g., '255, 0, 0' for red) or a hex code (e.g., 'ff0000' for red) (default setting: 200, 200, 200).
_comment_10: The 'Percentage of Cell Dimension that is Cropped' setting, with possible values between 1 and 100, will determine the width of the square cell cropping area that will be used to predict the color in every cell, expressed as a percentage of the square graph paper cell dimension. For example, a value of 50 would represent 50% of the square cell width or height. A setting between 25 and 75 works best, to ensure that enough pixels are included, while preventing the crop area from overspilling into neighboring cells. (default setting: 50).
_comment_11: The 'Number of Squares in Pixel Art Drawing Width', of which the value needs to be greater than zero, represents the total width of your final pixel art drawing, after the code automatically merges the individual 65x65 grids together, if applicable. For example, an image spanning two full grids in width would have a total width of 130 pixels in the unscaled PNG image (default setting: 65).
_comment_12: The 'Number of Squares in Pixel Art Drawing Height', of which the value needs to be greater than zero, represents the total height of your final pixel art drawing, after the code automatically merges the individual 65x65 grids together, if applicable. For example, an image spanning two full grids in height would have a total height of 130 pixels in the unscaled PNG image (default setting: 65).
_comment_13: The 'Scaling Factor', expressed in integer values above zero (e.g., 1, 2, 10, 20, etc.), represents the number of times that the pixel art will be scaled by to generate the final PNG image, with a scaling factor of one yielding the original size. For example, a scaling factor of 10 would convert an initial drawing of 65 x 65 graph paper squares to a 650 x 650 pixel PNG image (default value: 1).
_comment_14: 'Number of Colors Excluding White in Pixel Art Drawing', of which the value needs to be at least one, represents the number of colors used in the pixel art drawing and in the scanned color key, excluding white, which is the page color. For example, should the drawing include blue, red, green, and black colors and some squares that were left in the white paper color, a value of 4 would be used (default setting: 2).
_comment_15: The 'Grayscale Mode' will determine whether or not the Grayscale Mode is enabled, which leads to faster computation times if your drawing was either drawn or scanned in grayscale (default setting: False, or OFF).
